hints.title: Common Ancestor Distance Formula
hints.text: The path distance between p and q in a tree equals depth(p) + depth(q) - 2 * depth(ancestor).

hints.title: Finding Lowest Common Ancestor
hints.text: Locate the lowest common ancestor of nodes with values p and q using standard bottom-up tree recursion.

hints.title: Measuring Subtree Depths
hints.text: From the found ancestor, compute the downward distance to p and the downward distance to q and sum them.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in binary tree
complexity.notes: Finds LCA and measures descendant depths in at most two linear passes.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Graph conversion adds extra space and graph traversal overhead when tree hierarchy directly yields depths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: LCA-anchored depth computation uses O(H) recursion stack without graph allocation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: LCA location followed by depth distance summation.
